- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.10) over recent days, model tends to underpredict upward moves; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for the next 5–7 days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.20), model often overpredicts downward moves; adjust downward by 1–4% for the next 5–10 days.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply a 2–5 day “cool-down” correction, reducing forecast by 1–3% per day post-spike.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show model overpredicting (e.g., +2%+ above true), reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate true price peaks in late period (last 7–10 days); add 0.5–1.5% buffer to final 5–7 days if sentiment is positive.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– swings, model often fails to capture momentum shifts; use sentiment direction as signal to adjust forecast slope (e.g., +0.2% per day if sentiment > 0.15).
